studies.Study: van Alfen SJ et al. (2026) [PMID: 42100998] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Iron Status, Erythropoietin, and Cancer Incidence in the General Population.
studies.Title: Iron Status, Erythropoietin, and Cancer Incidence in the General Population.
studies.Authors: van Alfen SJ, Rawee P, Luo L, Nolte IM, van der Vegt B, Kootstra-Ros JE, Bakker SJL, Gansevoort RT, Links TP, Zandee WT, Eisenga MF
studies.Population: Community-dwelling individuals in the PREVEND cohort

sample_size.excerpt: Data were obtained from 6109 participants (mean age 52 ± 12 years; 49% male) in the Prevention of Renal and Vascular End‐stage Disease (PREVEND) cohort.

effect_size.excerpt: When looking at site‐specific cancer risk, the relationship between kidney cancer and log‐transformed ferritin (as a continuous variable) remained significant (HR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.2–0.67; p = 0.005), whereas the previously identified associations were not found to be statistically significant after adjusting for multiple testing.
effect_size.location: Results, Iron Status, EPO Levels, and Site‐Specific Cancer Risk, paragraph 2

confidence_interval.excerpt: When looking at site‐specific cancer risk, the relationship between kidney cancer and log‐transformed ferritin (as a continuous variable) remained significant (HR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.2–0.67; p = 0.005), whereas the previously identified associations were not found to be statistically significant after adjusting for multiple testing.
confidence_interval.location: Results, Iron Status, EPO Levels, and Site‐Specific Cancer Risk, paragraph 2

p_value.excerpt: Among non‐smokers, elevated sTfR levels were linked to increased cancer risk (HR, 1.68; 95% CI: 1.21–2.32; p = 0.002), a pattern not observed in smokers (HR, 0.81; 95% CI: 0.47–1.39; p = 0.5).
p_value.location: Results, Iron Status, EPO Levels, and Site‐Specific Cancer Risk, paragraph 2

comparison.excerpt: as compared to the lowest tertile of ferritin
comparison.location: Results, Iron Status, EPO Levels, and Site‐Specific Cancer Risk, paragraph 2

design.excerpt: For this prospective, observational study, we used the Prevention of Renal and Vascular End‐stage Disease (PREVEND) study, the details of which have been described elsewhere [ 12 ].
design.location: Methods, Study Design and Population, paragraph 1

timing.excerpt: Over a median follow‐up time of 18.5 (IQR, 15.4–18.9) years, 1090 community‐dwelling individuals developed a de novo malignancy.
timing.location: Results, Iron Status, EPO Levels, and Risk of Overall Cancer, paragraph 1

continent.excerpt: Thirdly, the cohort primarily consisted of Caucasians in the North of the Netherlands, which may limit generalizability [ 27 ].

ethnicity.excerpt: We included 6109 community‐dwelling individuals (age 52 ± 12 years; 49% males; 96% Caucasian)

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Iron biomarkers, including ferritin, transferrin saturation, soluble transferrin receptor (sTfR), hepcidin and EPO levels, were measured at baseline.

gender.excerpt: Data were obtained from 6109 participants (mean age 52 ± 12 years; 49% male) in the Prevention of Renal and Vascular End‐stage Disease (PREVEND) cohort.

smoking_status.excerpt: Multivariable analysis was adjusted for socio‐demographic factors (age, sex, race, education (low, middle, high), smoking (never, former, present), and alcohol consumption (never, moderate, severe))
